key: Behold, I have refined thee, but not as silver; I have tried thee in the furnace of affliction.
s: Midway through rebuking obstinate Jacob, the LORD recalls Israel’s trials; Radak, on 48:10, reads it as a refining short of the refiner’s, who removes all the dross, for had He done so few would have remained, the wicked afflicted but not wholly cut off.

evidence.gloss: But not as silver: not like a refiner of silver, for the refiner removes all the dross from the silver and consumes it until nothing but refined silver is left; I did not do so, for few would have remained had I done so; but the wicked among you, who are the dross, I afflicted with sicknesses, captivity, bereavement of children, or in the fruit of cattle or of the ground, as written in the curses, not to cut them off altogether.

reason: CORRECTED for both clarity faults, which hold: ‘since then few would have remained’ read first as time, and ‘his trials’ after ‘His name’s sake’ could be taken for the LORD’s own. The name aside is dropped, Israel is named (48:1 addresses the house of Jacob called by the name of Israel; 48:4 obstinate), and the condition is explicit (‘for had He done so few would have remained’, Radak’s כי מעטים היו הנשארים אם עשיתי כן), with ‘all the dross’ restored (כל הסיגים).
